author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Waymo plans to offer autonomous ride-hailing trips to the general public in Las Vegas, bringing Alphabet’s self-driving unit into Nevada’s market for paid robotaxi rides, Reuters reported Monday.

The service is expected to start with a few dozen vehicles before expanding. Waymo’s arrival gives Las Vegas another commercial autonomous-vehicle operator after Zoox began offering paid rides there last month.

Waymo has already expanded beyond its original California markets into parts of Texas, Florida and Arizona. The company was valued at $126 billion in February after raising $16 billion, according to Reuters, highlighting the scale of investor expectations around autonomous transportation.

Las Vegas is a high-profile test for robotaxis because of its tourism economy and dense travel corridors. Waymo will still face competition from Zoox and Tesla as companies work to prove that driverless services can operate safely, reliably and at a large enough scale to become a routine transportation option.
dek: Alphabet’s self-driving unit Waymo says it will open its Las Vegas ride-hailing service to the general public, adding Nevada to its growing robotaxi network.
headline: Waymo to bring public robotaxi rides to Las Vegas
